1:# Self-hosted short link tracking
2-
3-Short links embedded in social posts (for click attribution) use a self-hosted domain with a redirect endpoint and Redis-based counting — no external service like Bitly or Dub.
4-
5-**Why**: Short link clicks are the primary signal for Content Touch interactions in the Customer Graph. Routing these through a third-party service would either require callbacks to reconcile data (fragile) or accept that click data lives outside SpellPaw (defeating the unified data model). Self-hosting costs a domain registration and one API route (`/<code>` resolving to a redirect). At Phase 1 scale (≤ 100 monthly active Contacts, ≤ 50 published posts), the traffic volume is trivial. The value of owning the click data — mapping every click back to a specific Post and Contact — is the foundation of the Customer Graph's cross-channel reasoning.
6-
7-**Considered alternative**: Using an external short link service with webhook callbacks. Rejected because it introduces a third-party dependency for the most critical data pipeline in the product and creates a reconciliation gap whenever a webhook is missed.
8-
9-**Consequences**:
10-- Redirects are handled by Next.js Middleware (no React rendering overhead; < 30ms). Redis caches hot links; miss falls back to PostgreSQL.
11-- Click events are written via BullMQ fire-and-forget (3 retries, exponential backoff) — the redirect does not block on the Interaction write, but no click is silently lost.
12-- Hot links (freshly published posts) stay in Redis TTL 24h; after the traffic spike decays, lookups fall through to the DB naturally.
====
5:**Why**: The original concept ("an external-communication AI operating system for SMB and AI-native builders") left the value proposition unverifiable and the target user ambiguous. As built through M2, the product was indistinguishable from a multi-channel scheduling tool (a red ocean against Buffer/Hootsuite). The re-examination (grilling session, 2026-08-03) resolved six decisions: core value = lifecycle intelligence; primary persona = AI-native builders (micro-SMB secondary); first real channel = Twitter/X, inserted between M3 and M4 so M4 ships a real-data closed loop (real publish → real short-link clicks → Content Touch → Graph); M5 = release readiness (docs, E2E, deployment, perf/security, landing, English launch) instead of more features; Phase 1 limits are abuse guardrails (3 Channels / 50 Posts / 1000 Contacts, env-configurable) not a paywall, with pricing deferred until real usage data exists; product language = English primary, zh second.
6-
7:**Considered alternative**: Serving SMB marketing teams first for cash flow. Rejected because the repo's technical decisions were already irreversibly builder-leaning (BYOK — ADR-0005, embedded MCP — ADR-0010, self-hosted short links — ADR-0009), and a solo builder cannot run a sales-led SMB motion; product-led growth (docs, community, English launch) is the viable path. Keeping both personas as equals was also rejected — the intersection of their needs is the undifferentiated publishing tool.
8-
9:**Consequence**: M3–M5 scope is now fixed: M3 MCP + AI provider unchanged; X real integration lands before M4 (X API cost + developer review are a schedule risk to track); M4 delivers Graph with real data, analytics, i18n en/zh; M5 is release readiness with English-first narrative; M6+ is feedback-driven (Inbox Phase 1, analytics depth, orchestration are all candidates, in that order). Free-plan limits must be env-configurable guardrails, and the pricing model (BYOK + usage vs subscription) stays undecided until real usage distribution exists. Content Touch data quality now depends on the X integration — the mock adapters no longer represent the revenue-critical path.

3-Short links embedded in social posts (for click attribution) use a self-hosted domain with a redirect endpoint and Redis-based counting — no external service like Bitly or Dub.
4-
5-**Why**: Short link clicks are the primary signal for Content Touch interactions in the Customer Graph. Routing these through a third-party service would either require callbacks to reconcile data (fragile) or accept that click data lives outside SpellPaw (defeating the unified data model). Self-hosting costs a domain registration and one API route (`/<code>` resolving to a redirect). At Phase 1 scale (≤ 100 monthly active Contacts, ≤ 50 published posts), the traffic volume is trivial. The value of owning the click data — mapping every click back to a specific Post and Contact — is the foundation of the Customer Graph's cross-channel reasoning.
6-
7-**Considered alternative**: Using an external short link service with webhook callbacks. Rejected because it introduces a third-party dependency for the most critical data pipeline in the product and creates a reconciliation gap whenever a webhook is missed.
8-
9-**Consequences**:
10-- Redirects are handled by Next.js Middleware (no React rendering overhead; < 30ms). Redis caches hot links; miss falls back to PostgreSQL.
11-- Click events are written via BullMQ fire-and-forget (3 retries, exponential backoff) — the redirect does not block on the Interaction write, but no click is silently lost.
12-- Hot links (freshly published posts) stay in Redis TTL 24h; after the traffic spike decays, lookups fall through to the DB naturally.
====
5:**Why**: The original concept ("an external-communication AI operating system for SMB and AI-native builders") left the value proposition unverifiable and the target user ambiguous. As built through M2, the product was indistinguishable from a multi-channel scheduling tool (a red ocean against Buffer/Hootsuite). The re-examination (grilling session, 2026-08-03) resolved six decisions: core value = lifecycle intelligence; primary persona = AI-native builders (micro-SMB secondary); first real channel = Twitter/X, inserted between M3 and M4 so M4 ships a real-data closed loop (real publish → real short-link clicks → Content Touch → Graph); M5 = release readiness (docs, E2E, deployment, perf/security, landing, English launch) instead of more features; Phase 1 limits are abuse guardrails (3 Channels / 50 Posts / 1000 Contacts, env-configurable) not a paywall, with pricing deferred until real usage data exists; product language = English primary, zh second.
6-
7:**Considered alternative**: Serving SMB marketing teams first for cash flow. Rejected because the repo's technical decisions were already irreversibly builder-leaning (BYOK — ADR-0005, embedded MCP — ADR-0010, self-hosted short links — ADR-0009), and a solo builder cannot run a sales-led SMB motion; product-led growth (docs, community, English launch) is the viable path. Keeping both personas as equals was also rejected — the intersection of their needs is the undifferentiated publishing tool.
8-
9:**Consequence**: M3–M5 scope is now fixed: M3 MCP + AI provider unchanged; X real integration lands before M4 (X API cost + developer review are a schedule risk to track); M4 delivers Graph with real data, analytics, i18n en/zh; M5 is release readiness with English-first narrative; M6+ is feedback-driven (Inbox Phase 1, analytics depth, orchestration are all candidates, in that order). Free-plan limits must be env-configurable guardrails, and the pricing model (BYOK + usage vs subscription) stays undecided until real usage distribution exists. Content Touch data quality now depends on the X integration — the mock adapters no longer represent the revenue-critical path.
